question: What is the percentage of the population with access to clean fuels and technology for cooking in the Sustainable Development Report 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**74%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report 2025**, which tracks the global progress toward the **United Nations' 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, indicates that approximately **74%** of the global population has access to **clean fuels and technologies for cooking**.
 
• This indicator is a primary metric for monitoring **SDG 7**, which aims to ensure **access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy** for all people by the **year 2030**.
 
• Access to clean cooking involves the transition from traditional fuels like **wood, charcoal, and coal** to cleaner alternatives such as **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)**, **natural gas**, **electricity**, and **biogas**.
 
• The report highlights that while there has been significant progress in regions like **Central and Southern Asia**, a large "access gap" remains in **Sub-Saharan Africa**, where traditional biomass is still widely used.
 
• Ensuring **74%** access marks a critical step, yet the **2025 report** emphasizes that current trajectories are not yet sufficient to reach the **100% target** set for **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7):**
 
 
• The goal focuses on three main pillars: **universal access to modern energy**, increasing the **renewable energy share** in the global mix, and doubling the global rate of **energy efficiency** improvement.
 
• Energy is central to nearly every major challenge and opportunity the world faces today, including **poverty alleviation**, **food security**, and **climate change mitigation**.
 
 
 
• **Health and Environmental Impacts:**
 
 
• Lack of clean cooking facilities leads to **household air pollution**, which the **World Health Organization (WHO)** identifies as a leading cause of **premature deaths** globally.
 
• Switching to clean fuels reduces **carbon emissions** and prevents **deforestation** caused by the excessive harvesting of firewood.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report** is produced annually by the **SDSN**, an initiative launched in **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General**.
 
• It provides the **SDG Index** and **Dashboards**, which assess the performance of all **193 UN Member States** in implementing the **2030 Agenda**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Classifications:** To be considered "clean," technologies must meet specific **emission standards** defined by **WHO guidelines** for indoor air quality.
 
• **Data Sources:** The figures in the **Sustainable Development Report 2025** are aggregated using data from the **International Energy Agency (IEA)**, the **World Bank**, and the **World Health Organization (WHO)**.
 
• **Gender Dimension:** Women and children are disproportionately affected by the lack of clean fuels, as they are typically responsible for **fuel collection** and are most exposed to **indoor smoke**.
 
• **Global Target:** Achieving universal access (**100%**) requires an estimated **annual investment** of billions of dollars, particularly in infrastructure for **electricity grids** and **fuel distribution** in rural areas.
